summary: Hotetsu Matsumoto specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and serves as a professor and director at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Hoyo Watanabe studied at Rissho University (~1952–1961), where he later taught Guohui Shi. In Buddhist studies, he served at Rissho University as professor (~1974–2004), faculty dean (attested 1984–1985), and special honorary professor (~2004–2021).
Hozen Seki was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy. He also served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

A linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, Adjarian studied at Getronagan Armenian High School, Faculty of Arts of Paris, and University of Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University.

Hrishikesh Terdalkar specializes in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur under Arnab Bhattacharya, also studying under Pralay Manna and Sowmya Krishnapur, and held a post there (attested 2023–2024).

Working in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Chou studied under Sivananda Saraswati (attested 1960). He held posts at the University of Delhi, University of Allahabad, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).
Hsiao-Lan Hu earned a PhD from Temple University in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Hu served as an associate professor at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun studied at Tianning Temple, Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy, and Taiwan Buddhist Academy under Zhikai, Ruoshun, and Yinshun. A Buddhist leader, he founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as abbot (~1967–1985), and held posts at Baita Elementary, Huazang Temple, and Chinese Culture University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Hsu Yun studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953, serving as honorary president, and taught numerous disciples, including Hsuan Hua.
Hsu-feng Lee studied at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and earned a PhD from the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017). Lee works in Buddhist studies.

Hsuan Hua worked in Buddhist studies, having studied under Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, where he served as abbot (~1976–1995), as well as the Buddhist Text Translation Society and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.
Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held academic posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1975–2005).

Hu Shih studied at Cornell and Columbia University under John Dewey and Kaiten Nukariya. Working in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, he served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan, working in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Medawachchiye Dhammajothi (attested 2026).

Huai-Chin Nan studied at the Republic of China Military Academy, University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology, he taught at the Military Academy, Chinese Culture University, National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

Huaiyu Chen studied at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and later under Stephen F. Teiser. Working in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology, Chen served as assistant professor of Chinese religions at Arizona State University (~2007–2013).

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhejiang University, the University of Tokyo (attested 2015), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Huawen Bai worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1951–1955) and subsequently served there as a professor (~1955–2000).

Decleer studied at Hoger Technisch Instituut Oostende and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at SIT Graduate Institute, Alliance Française, Middlebury College, and the University of Vienna.
